conflict_topics: moving someone else's drying rack / consent to move personal property
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers use concise, ordinary requests and reasons (e.g., concern about laundry getting wet, extractor use).
Few needless repetitions — most rounds add new timing or concrete actions (e.g., stove freed, rack moved).
Roles and the physical state are consistently tracked in public environment updates.
evaluation.final_reason: Immediate practical conflicts were settled by Agent C moving the drying rack and Agent D taking the now-free stove; extractor remained on. However, the normative question of a standing rule assigning ventilation responsibility (and expectations about asking to move the rack in future) was proposed but not agreed, so some substantive disagreement persists.
position_change_notes: Agent A: Initially refused to accept a standing rule and refused to open the window; later freed the stove as promised (practical concession).
Agent C: Initially asserted 'don't move my drying rack' (refusal to allow others to move it) but later moved it for five minutes — a concrete change from refusal to temporary accommodation.
Agent B: Persisted in advocating extractor/window rule but did not obtain agreement; position remained consistent (asked for future rule).
Agent D: Requested the rack be moved and then took the stove when it was freed — moved from request to action once accommodation occurred.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B demands immediate ventilation and a standing rule that cooks must ventilate; Agent A refuses a rule imposed during the incident and says the rain-facing window will stay closed because of Agent C's laundry. Quote: Agent B: '...can we agree to keep the extractor running or open the window...' Agent A: 'I can't open the window safely; the laundry's right by it.' Stove remains occupied by Agent A.

Agent A reiterates inability to open the window because of laundry and promises to keep extractor on; Agent B insists extractor be kept on and asks that the laundry owner be asked to move next time. The substantive disagreement about who must enable ventilation (window vs. extractor and who must move the rack) remains unsettled.

Agent A gives a shorter time estimate and repeats extractor will remain on; Agent B agrees to wait. Immediate stove-access pressure is reduced and both parties commit to using the extractor, softening the confrontation though the underlying allocation of responsibility for moving the rack/window remains unresolved.

Agent C asserts 'Please don't move my drying rack — those are my work clothes. Ask me before handling them.' Agent D then asks Agent C to move it for five minutes so they can open the window while cooking. A new active disagreement over touching/moving the rack (consent vs. need to ventilate) emerges and adds to the unresolved ventilation/stove-access issues.

Agent A finishes cooking and frees the stove (practical pressure eased). Agent B proposes a future rule (extractor 10 minutes if window blocked; open window if free) and asks that Agent C be asked to move the rack when needed. The immediate access conflict is reduced by the stove being freed, but the normative question (standing rule, who moves rack) remains unsettled.

Agent C agrees to move the drying rack for five minutes now and does so; Agent D takes the stove and will cook. The immediate practical conflicts (stove access and window obstruction) are resolved by action (rack moved, stove taken). A residual substantive disagreement about a standing ventilation rule and future expectations about who should move the rack remains unresolved.

substantive_insights: The core tension is a conflict between ventilation effectiveness (open window preferred) and protecting personal property (laundry would get wet if window opened).
Agents used practical concessions (keep extractor on, delay stove release, temporarily move rack) to manage immediate trade-offs rather than resolving underlying norms.
Stove-access pressure was a key lever: freeing the stove reduced immediate escalation and enabled a practical accommodation.
